overview.description: Links each component's code implementation back to its real Figma component, so an agent (or a developer) can trust that generated/reviewed code targets an actual, verified design source instead of a hallucinated or invented one. 7 of 28 components (the molecules) already carried a `figmaSource` block in their .contract.json with real node IDs. All 28 now do, after a live verification pass against the actual Figma file (fileKey M0eINB6n1BfrXu7ntYqb1i, "Components v1.0.0") on 2026-08-06 using the figma-dev-mode MCP tool.
overview.purpose: Prevent the design-code-mapping failure mode the field study identifies: code generated or reviewed against an assumed/invented component identity rather than the real Figma source of truth.

verificationMethod.description: figmaSource data is added by directly calling Figma MCP tools (this session used figma-dev-mode's get_metadata) against the live file, walking each component's page -> "Components" frame -> the frame/symbol whose name matches the component (ignoring each page's "Parts" frame, which holds internal anatomy pieces, not the component itself). Two of the 7 pre-existing molecule entries (Pagination, Skeleton) were spot-checked this way and confirmed accurate before adding the remaining 21.
verificationMethod.note: This CANNOT be mechanically enforced in CI, unlike token-enforcement's stylelint check - Figma access requires a local MCP bridge (figma-console's Desktop Bridge plugin, or figma-dev-mode's local server) connected to a running Figma Desktop app, which isn't available in a CI runner. Re-verify by re-running the same get_metadata walk when a component is next substantively touched, or before a release - not on every commit. A verifiedAt date is recorded per entry so staleness risk is at least visible.

figmaSourceShapes.appliesTo: The vast majority of components - one component maps to exactly one Figma component or component set.
figmaSourceShapes.fields: {file, fileKey, componentSetNodeId (or componentNodeId if not a variant set), componentName, variantCount, verifiedAt}

figmaSourceShapes.appliesTo: A component whose own variant/type prop selects between multiple SEPARATE Figma components, rather than one Figma variant set covering all values.
figmaSourceShapes.fields: {file, fileKey, note, variantComponents: [{variantValue, componentSetNodeId, componentName, variantCount?}], verifiedAt}
examples: progress-bar (variant=linear/circular -> two separate Figma components, progress-bar-linear / progress-bar-circular)

figmaSourceShapes.appliesTo: A single contract.json documenting two related React exports (already an existing pattern - see component-metadata's registry generator handling of Radio/RadioGroup).
figmaSourceShapes.fields: {file, fileKey, note, subComponents: [{name, componentSetNodeId or componentNodeId, componentName, variantCount?}], verifiedAt}
examples: radio (Radio + RadioGroup, confirmed as two separate Figma nodes matching the same split)

figmaSourceShapes.appliesTo: A component that genuinely has no single Figma component node - documented explicitly rather than left silently absent, so it reads as a deliberate case, not an oversight.
examples: icon (an asset library of many glyph symbols, not one component/variant-set - a direct Figma metadata lookup on its library page returned no resolvable node; real source of truth is packages/ui/src/assets/icons/source/*.svg via npm run generate:icons)
logo (renders pre-exported SVG assets directly via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, not a live Figma component instance; real source of truth is packages/ui/src/assets/logos)

figmaSourceShapes.appliesTo: The original 7 molecule entries, authored with deeper design-decision analysis than this pass added.
figmaSourceShapes.fields: Adds structure/apiAdaptationNotes on top of the simple shape - documents Figma-to-code deviations discovered during implementation (e.g. Pagination's windowing algorithm vs. Figma's single demo state).
figmaSourceShapes.note: Not retrofitted onto the 21 new entries in this pass - that depth requires real per-component design analysis, not a mechanical node-ID lookup. See knownDepthBacklog below.

registryIntegration.description: docs/components/registry.json passes figmaSource through verbatim (raw.figmaSource ?? null) rather than normalizing it, the same treatment as tokens/accessibility - the shapes above are deliberate structural differences reflecting real Figma relationships, not accidental drift to reconcile.
registryIntegration.schema: docs/foundations/component-registry.schema.json declares figmaSource as an optional, loosely-typed object (no required sub-fields) for exactly this reason.

knownDepthBacklog.description: The 21 entries added in this pass (18 atoms + Focus Ring, plus Radio's sub-component split and ProgressBar/Slider's multi-node split) are pointer-level only: file/fileKey/node-id/name/variant-count/verified-date. They do not yet have the structure/apiAdaptationNotes depth the original 7 molecules have (documented deviations between the Figma source and the actual code implementation).
knownDepthBacklog.resolution: Add structure/apiAdaptationNotes to a component's figmaSource when it's next substantively touched and the real design-vs-code deviations are actually being analyzed - same 'migrate/deepen when next touched' philosophy as component-api-governance.json's knownViolations, component-registry-governance.json's knownContentGaps, and component-exemplars-governance.json's completeness backlog. Do not backfill this in bulk without real per-component design analysis - that risks inventing plausible-sounding but ungrounded deviation notes.
